THE EPISTLE TO THE ROMANS. I. 1-7. THE APOSTOLIC SALUTATION. Paul, a devoted servant of Jesus Christ, an Apostle called and set apart to preach the Gospel of God, sends greeting to the Christians of Rome, beloved of God and called to be saints. 1-7. In writing to the Church of the imperial city, which he had not yet visited, St. Paul delivers his credentials with some solemnity. I. IlavXor. The name Paul first appears in Acts xiii. 9; it is a Roman cognomen which the Apostle bore from his birth, con- currently with his Jewish name Saul, and not one assumed later. δοῦλος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. The word denotes absolute ownership, and is chosen here as in Phil. i. 1 with a marked sense of humility.
